behaviorDesc: Pads silently along game trails, swims rivers without a ripple. It has already decided about you long before you see it.
description: a powerfully built spotted cat with eyes that found you first
diseaseVector: Apex predator — the danger is the teeth, not disease. Butcher away from camp; the smell of blood draws others.
huntText: The trail goes quiet — too quiet. Then the undergrowth exhales, and the rosettes resolve into muscle, ten feet away, already moving.
killText: About {kcal} kcal of dense meat, plus a hide worth real trade. It answered your missed strike — next time, don't miss. Or better: don't take the shot you're not sure of.

knowledgeLevels.1: Jaguar. Spots, muscle, eyes that found you first.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich), hide (trade), bones (tools), teeth (trade). It swims and climbs — nowhere is safe near water at dusk.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the region's apex. A missed strike brings the maul — it answers at range 2. Fire and noise hold it; turning your back invites it.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: it bites through skulls (turtles, caiman, you). Hunt it only with a party and a plan, or better yet, hunt around it — the forest is big enough for both of you.

name: Jaguar
tell: the birds stop mid-call — then a single coughing sawing roar, too close
unknown: a spotted weight moving through the understory, utterly silent

behaviorDesc: Grazes the water's edge in herds, always one head up. Barks an alarm and the whole herd is in the river before you blink.
description: a barrel-bodied giant rodent, half-submerged, watching you with total calm
diseaseVector: Water's edge animal — cook the meat through; wetland parasites are real.
huntText: It watches you from the shallows, unimpressed. The herd grazes on, one head always up — you get one clean approach before the barking starts.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the world's largest rodent eats like pork and feeds a crowd. Gut fast in this heat.

knowledgeLevels.1: Capybara. Giant guinea pig, loves the water.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (a lot, pork-like), hide (tough leather). Herds of a dozen — where there's one, there are more.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the best meat-per-effort in the wetlands. They bark an alarm and dive — cut off the water and they panic.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: hunt at dawn when they graze out of the water. The herd always posts a lookout; take the lookout first and the rest freeze.

name: Capybara
tell: a sharp dog-like bark — then splashing as the herd hits the water
unknown: a barrel shape at the water's edge, placid and enormous

behaviorDesc: Hops the forest floor in pairs, stuffing its cheek pouches with fallen fruit. Freezes at danger, then explodes into the undergrowth.
description: a large grizzled rodent hopping through the leaf litter, cheeks stuffed
huntText: It freezes mid-hop, one paw up, cheek pouches bulging with palm fruit. You have until it decides you're a jaguar.
killText: About {kcal} kcal of lean meat. And check its cheek pouches — agoutis carry Brazil nuts they haven't buried yet.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean, good). Check the cheek pouches and buries — they hoard Brazil nuts.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the forest's gardener — it buries nuts and forgets them, planting the next generation of Brazil nut trees. Follow an agouti and find dinner twice.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: agoutis are creatures of habit with fixed trails. Snare the trail, not the animal. Pairs mate for life — where there's one, the partner is close.

name: Red-rumped Agouti
tell: a sharp staccato barking, then silence — it's watching from cover
unknown: a grizzled shape bobbing through the leaf litter

behaviorDesc: Moves in nervous herds, clicking their teeth in alarm. A cornered herd doesn't flee — it charges, and the tusks are the argument.
description: a bristly pig-like herd animal with a pale collar, teeth clicking in alarm
diseaseVector: Herd animal — cook the meat through.
huntText: The herd materializes from the thicket, collars flashing white. Teeth click like castanets — the big boar is deciding whether you're worth charging.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — musky, strong, and it feeds everyone. The scent gland on the back ruins the meat if you nick it; cut wide around it.

knowledgeLevels.1: Peccary. Pig-like, collared, travels in herds.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (musky — remove the scent gland on the back first, wide cut), hide.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: herds of 5-15. Never shoot into the middle of a nervous herd — a wounded peccary herd charges.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: the clicking teeth are the warning. Take the trailing animal with a clean shot and the herd runs past you, not over you.

name: Collared Peccary
tell: teeth clicking like castanets, getting faster
unknown: bristly shapes moving through the thicket, clicking

behaviorDesc: Crosses the canopy in pairs, screaming. Lands to eat clay at the riverbank licks — the one predictable thing about it.
description: a huge scarlet-and-blue parrot screaming across the canopy
huntText: The scream comes first — then scarlet and blue tearing across the canopy gap. It lands at the clay lick, wary, tasting the mud between screams.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — mostly a trophy of patience. The long tail feathers are trade wealth; the beak cracks Brazil nuts.

knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: they eat clay at riverbank licks to neutralize toxins in unripe fruit — find the lick and you find the birds, every morning.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: pairs for life and holds a territory. Learn one pair's route and you can predict them to the hour. Snare the lick, not the sky.

name: Scarlet Macaw
tell: a harsh rolling scream — 'raaa!' — twice, from the canopy
unknown: a scream and a flash of scarlet over the trees

behaviorDesc: Hops branch to branch, tossing its ridiculous beak around like it weighs nothing. Wary of everything, curious about everything.
description: a black bird with a snow-white throat and an enormous orange beak
huntText: It tilts its head, the orange beak catching the light like a lantern. One hop closer — then it decides you're a hawk and the whole treetop empties.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a mouthful, honestly. But the beak is a curiosity worth trade, and the white throat feathers are beautiful.

knowledgeLevels.1: Toco toucan. Huge orange beak, white throat.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the beak is a radiator — it dumps heat. Toucans follow fruiting trees; find the fruit and you find the flock.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they're nest-robbers too — other birds mob them. Watch for the mob and you'll find the toucan before it finds you.

name: Toco Toucan
tell: a deep frog-like croaking — 'grrrak' — from high in the canopy
unknown: a flash of white throat and orange among the leaves

behaviorDesc: Sits high and roars at dawn — a chorus you feel in your chest a kilometer away. Troops move slow and predictable through the canopy.
description: a rust-red monkey with a black beard, roaring at the dawn
diseaseVector: Primates share our diseases — cook thoroughly, handle with care.
huntText: The dawn chorus finds you first — a roar like wind through a canyon, impossibly loud. The troop moves through the canopy above, slow, watching.
killText: About {kcal} kcal of strong meat. The troop will remember this tree — don't hunt the same troop twice in a week.

knowledgeLevels.1: Howler monkey. Red, bearded, deafening at dawn.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: the dawn chorus carries for kilometers — you can map every troop in earshot without moving. They sleep in the same trees.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: troops move slow along fixed canopy highways. Ambush the route at dawn, not the animal at noon. Take one; the troop relocates for days.

name: Red Howler Monkey
tell: the dawn roar — a deep guttural chorus that vibrates your ribs
unknown: a rust-red shape in the high canopy, roaring

behaviorDesc: A living boulder on the trail at night, snuffling. Near-blind but nose-led; it will walk right past you if the wind is right — or right over you if it isn't.
description: a huge dark barrel of an animal with a short trunk, snuffling along the trail
diseaseVector: Large game — gut fast in the heat, cook through.
huntText: The trail trembles. It emerges like a boulder that decided to walk — trunk testing the air, tiny eyes seeing nothing, nose seeing everything.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the biggest land animal in South America feeds a village for days. The hide is armor-thick; the meat is rich and dark.

knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: salt licks and river crossings are the ambush points — tapirs are creatures of deep habit.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: it hears poorly and sees worse, but the nose is everything. Hunt downwind or don't hunt. A deadfall on a tapir trail is the patient hunter's answer.

name: Lowland Tapir
tell: a high whistling snort in the dark, then heavy footfalls
unknown: a boulder that breathes, moving along the night trail

behaviorDesc: Rolls at the surface to breathe — a torpedo of muscle gulping air. The roll is the tell; the harpoon answers it.
description: a massive armored fish rolling at the surface, gulping air
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: The surface bulges — then a head the size of a bucket breaks water, mouth gaping for air. It rolls, armored scales flashing red at the edges, and is gone.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the Amazon's king fish, a hundred kilos of meat on one spear. The tongue is bone; the scales are armor plates.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (a mountain of it), tongue (bony — a tool), scales (armor, scrapers).
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: it MUST surface to breathe — watch for the roll in the dry season when the lakes shrink. Harpoon the roll.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: in the flood it disperses into the forest; in the dry it concentrates in the lakes. Fish the dry-season lakes and one pirarucu feeds the village for a week. The bony tongue was the traditional grater — use it.

name: Pirarucu
tell: a deep rolling gulp at the surface — then silence
unknown: a vast shape rolling just under the black water

behaviorDesc: Cruises the flooded forest in schools, crunching fallen fruit. In the flood season the forest feeds the fish and the fish feed you.
description: a deep-bodied silver fish with human-like teeth, crunching fallen fruit
diseaseVector: Raw freshwater fish can carry parasites. Cook it.
huntText: Fruit plops into the black water — and the surface erupts. Silver bodies roll and crunch, teeth like molars grinding palm nuts to paste.
killText: About {kcal} kcal of rich oily meat — the flood season's gift. The ribs are the best eating in the river.

knowledgeLevels.1: Tambaqui. Big silver fruit-eater with weird teeth.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: in the flood it eats what the forest drops — bait your hook with fruit, not worms. Palm nuts are candy to it.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: the flood pulse is the calendar — as waters rise, tambaqui move into the forest; as they fall, they crowd the channels. Fish the falling water.

name: Tambaqui
tell: loud crunching and splashing under fruiting trees after a plop
unknown: silver flashes and crunching under the flooded trees

behaviorDesc: Holds the creek pool in a shimmering school, nervous and quick. Mostly a scavenger — until blood hits the water, and then it isn't.
description: a small deep-bodied fish with an underbite full of triangular teeth
diseaseVector: Sharp teeth, not disease. Cook as usual.
huntText: The school hangs in the current, fins flickering — a hundred small red bellies. They scatter at your shadow and reform behind you, curious.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small, bony, and delicious fried crisp. Catch a dozen and it's a meal. Mind the teeth when unhooking.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (fry whole and crisp). The jaws are a curiosity.
knowledgeLevels.3: Uses: mostly scavengers — the frenzy stories need blood and panic. Don't swim with open wounds; don't thrash.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they're a food source, not a horror. A line with meat scraps in a creek pool fills a basket by dusk. The teeth make excellent small blades.

name: Red-bellied Piranha
tell: a nervous shimmer as the school turns as one
unknown: a shimmer of red bellies in the creek
